items.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
items.description: The Danish prime minister has accused Russia of "reckless" behaviour, while the Kremlin is yet to comment.

items.title: What weapon could the US have put into space?
items.description: The announcement by the US points to a developing field of modern warfare in the Earth's orbit.

items.title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption
items.description: Trains were cancelled or delayed on Tuesday after objects were found on tracks at multiple locations.

items.title: Two sailors missing after tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Oman says
items.description: Iran says El Gaia caught fire after hitting mines, but the US says the oil tanker was struck by a missile and then a drone.

items.title: Iran war has led to US munitions shortfalls, Pentagon inspector confirms
items.description: The inspector also found a bottleneck in resupply, despite President Donald Trump's claims that US supplies are "virtually limitless".

items.title: Canada is a 'safe harbour' for global finance, Carney says
items.description: The prime minister is hosting a major global investment summit, with the goal of attracting money into the country amid a trade war with the US.

items.title: Ed Sheeran says it was 'not my decision' to drop Macklemore from tour
items.description: The star says tour promoters took the decision, after Macklemore made pro-Palestinian statements on stage.

items.title: Ash from Mount Etna grounds flights at Sicily airport
items.description: All flights are suspended from one of Italy's busiest airports until Tuesday night.

items.title: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys makes Emmy Awards history with double win
items.description: He becomes the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night at the prestigious TV ceremony.

items.title: British woman abducted in Malawi, police say
items.description: The mother of two young children was kidnapped in the middle of the day in the main city, Blantyre.

items.title: More than 100,000 people in Japan are now aged 100 or older
items.description: Figures show 88% of the centenarians are women as the population continues to age and shrink.

items.title: Colombian ex-foreign minister charged over nanny's lie detector test
items.description: Laura Sarabia is accused of ordering police to interrogate her nanny after cash allegedly went missing from her flat.

items.title: Nato jets down drone that entered Lithuanian airspace
items.description: The origin of the drone is currently unknown, but authorities say it likely entered Lithuania from neighbouring Belarus, an ally of Russia.

items.title: Donald Trump Jr and Bettina Trump say Putin ally paid for some wedding festivities as a 'gift'
items.description: An Instagram post from the couple said two nights of their wedding festivities in the Bahamas were partially funded by Umar Kremlev.

items.title: AI regulation faces political deadlock as calls grow for Congress to act
items.description: With Trump opposed and Congress divided, new safety legislation on AI is unlikely to pass anytime soon despite mounting pressure.

items.title: Legendary costume designer Bob Mackie dies aged 87
items.description: The "Sultan of Sequins" created iconic and dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John.

items.title: Wild dogs record 2,500-mile trek across Zambia in search of a mate
items.description: Scientists say the record-breaking journey by three brothers offers hope wildlife can survive growing pressures.

items.title: Satellite image reveals major damage that shut crucial oil pipeline
items.description: Experts tell BBC Verify the pipeline's closure could cut oil supplies by as much as 3.6 million barrels per day.

items.title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire
items.description: The state post service delivers pensions, medicine and letters to people just miles from the front.

items.title: Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion
items.description: Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.
